svg.title: Frontal entry and return through basal ganglia and thalamus
svg.desc: Three-panel schematic of macaque anatomy. Panel A shows four frontal source families (OFC/vmPFC, dACC, DLPFC, and pre-SMA/SMA/cingulate motor) projecting to a schematic sheet of striatal fields. Each family has a denser focal field and a lighter diffuse field; some fields overlap and others stay separate, and a note states that overlapping fields do not prove convergence on the same cells. Panel B arranges prefrontal and medial motor territories across the top, the striatum on the left, the GPi and SNr output nuclei below, and the thalamus (MD and VA/VL) on the right. Dorsal/rostral striatum projects to GPi and SNr, with a dashed route labelled via GPe/STN summarizing indirect circuitry; ventral striatum projects to ventral pallidum, which projects to MD. GPi projects to VA/VL and to the pedunculopontine nucleus; SNr projects to MD and to the superior colliculus. Prefrontal territories and MD, and medial motor territories and VA/VL, are linked by pairs of offset arrows in both directions that bypass the basal ganglia, so the routes return to the same cortical nodes. Panel C shows a single local example: an SMA subregion projects to a sampled VLo site, with no matching return field detected at that site. Arrows show direction only; synaptic signs are omitted.

g.text: No matching return field detected here.
Arrows show direction; synaptic signs omitted.
